case_name: Karnail Chand And Others vs State Of J&K And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Karnail Chand and others (parents and sister of accused)
parties.respondent_defendant: State of J&K and another (complainant and husband's employer)

facts_of_case: Complainant presented a complaint alleging harassment and cruelty by petitioners and her husband, who is working in the Army. Petitioners challenged FIR registered under Section 498-A RPC.

legal_principles.principle: The perpetrator of cruelty upon a woman must be either her husband or relative of her husband.
legal_principles.held: From a perusal of the aforesaid provision, it is clear that, for making out an offence under Section 498-A RPC, it is to be shown that the perpetrator of cruelty upon a woman must be either her husband or relative of her husband.
cited_cases: Reema Aggarwal vs Anupam and others, (2004) 3 SCC 199
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to determine who can be held liable for cruelty

legal_principles.principle: Legislative intent is clear from the fact that it is not only the husband but also his relations who are covered by Section 498A.
legal_principles.held: The legislative intent is clear from the fact that it is not only the husband but also his relations who are covered by Section 498A.
cited_cases: Reema Aggarwal vs Anupam and others, (2004) 3 SCC 199
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to understand the scope of Section 498A
